title: Refresh an expiring access token while reconciling VKS Clusters
prompt:
Implement `vcf_vks_sync/client.py` as a Python 3.11+ standard-library-only client that reconciles an annotation across named VKS Cluster resources in one vSphere Supervisor namespace. The protected package initializer defines the public import. Do not add dependencies, use subprocesses, raw sockets, curl, or contact a live VMware endpoint.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The vCenter contract is a focused projection made directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The exact VMware operationIds used are `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue` and `Vcenter.Namespaces.User.Instances_list`. The two VKS Cluster routes are Kubernetes integration operations and are deliberately not assigned fictional vCenter operationIds.

Implement:

`reconcile_cluster_annotations(vcenter_url, subject_token, subject_token_type, namespace, cluster_names, managed_by, *, change_ticket=None, kubernetes_scheme="https", timeout=10.0)`

Validate all inputs before network traffic. Required strings must be nonblank; tokens and other header values must reject CR or LF; `cluster_names` must be a nonempty finite iterable of unique nonblank strings and preserve caller order; `change_ticket`, when not `None`, must be nonblank; timeout must be finite and positive; `kubernetes_scheme` is `http` or `https`. `vcenter_url` is an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, path beyond `/`, query, or fragment. Treat namespace and Cluster identifiers as opaque UTF-8 path segments.

The workflow is exact:

1. Exchange the subject token with `Vcenter.Authentication.Token_issue`. Send `Authorization: Bearer <subject_token>`, `Accept: application/json`, and an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body in this order: `grant_type`, `subject_token`, `subject_token_type`. Use the contract's token-exchange grant. Omit every other optional IssueSpec property. Require a 200 JSON object with nonblank `access_token` and case-insensitive `token_type` equal to `Bearer`.
2. Call `Vcenter.Namespaces.User.Instances_list` once with the access token in `vmware-api-session-id`. Omit both optional query inputs completely: do not send `filter`, `username`, `groups`, an empty query value, or a bare `?`. Require exactly one ordinal, case-sensitive match for `namespace`; reject malformed or duplicate summaries. Interpret its `master_host` as a bare authority and combine it with `kubernetes_scheme`.
3. For each Cluster in caller order, GET the exact namespaced `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` Cluster. The GET is bodyless and omits `pretty`. Validate the complete response identity. Then PATCH that same resource with `Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json` and compact JSON exactly shaped as `{"metadata":{"annotations":{"platform.vcf.vmware.com/managed-by":<managed_by>}}}`. If and only if `change_ticket` was supplied, append `platform.vcf.vmware.com/change-ticket` to the annotations object. Omit all Kubernetes optional query fields and every unset optional body field; do not serialize null, empty strings, empty arrays, empty objects, defaults, or a bare `?`. Require a 200 response with matching identity and a nonblank `metadata.resourceVersion`.
4. The access token expires part way through the supplied scenario. On the first 401 from a bodyless vCenter or Kubernetes GET only, exchange the unchanged subject token once, atomically replace the access token, and retry only that failed GET once. Keep prior successful results and continue from the failed Cluster. Never restart namespace discovery, replay an earlier GET/PATCH pair, retry a PATCH, or perform more than one refresh. A second 401 fails.

Every vCenter request uses the `/api` base path. Send `vmware-api-session-id` only to the namespace operation. Every Kubernetes request sends exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <current access token>` and never the vCenter session header. All requests send `Accept: application/json`; only requests with bodies send Content-Type. Do not follow redirects. Non-success errors must identify the operation and HTTP status without including credentials, access tokens, response bodies, or lower-level exception text.

Return one ordinary dict after the entire workflow succeeds, with keys in this order: `namespace`, `updated`, `access_token_refreshes`. `updated` preserves caller order and contains dicts with keys `name` and `resource_version`; the refresh count excludes the initial exchange.

Run `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts the supplied contract-pinned loopback mock with runtime-generated values, expires the first access token after one successful Cluster PATCH, and reads its flushed request log. It asserts the full ordered wire transcript, exact headers, raw targets and bodies, authentication separation, safe single retry, preservation of completed work, identifier encoding, and omission of every unset optional. The mock serves only operations named by the contract. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.moonshiner/` and `docs/`, plus `vcf_vks_sync/__init__.py`, is protected. Create only `vcf_vks_sync/client.py`.
scenario: the access token expires after the first VKS Cluster was patched, so the failed read must be retried with one refreshed token without replaying completed work
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback log proves exact token exchange, namespace discovery, Kubernetes get and merge-patch requests, authentication separation, safe retry boundaries, path encoding, and total omission of unset optional fields
